indicators.note: arrangements of a word are new orders of its letters, so the next word is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up different ways to organise a pause in proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangements' tells you to rearrange the letters of ALTERNATIVE. A TEA INTERVAL is the break in a cricket match taken in the afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause for tea during a long game or working day is a break.

explanation.surface: Someone describing a surface that is both level and right-angled.
explanation.definitionFit: Level ground is flat, and two people who are quits after settling a debt are square.

parts.note: a flag is a waterside flower of this family, and the name is that of the Greek goddess of the rainbow, hence many colours

explanation.walkthrough: 'flag' reads as a banner, but a yellow flag is a wild plant of this genus, whose name comes from the rainbow goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden plant whose wild form is called a flag has blooms in many hues, as its rainbow-goddess name suggests.

clue.text: They supply brewed drinks on tap

definitions.text: They supply brewed drinks on tap

parts.words: They supply brewed drinks on tap
parts.note: 'on tap' suggests beer in a pub, but these large vessels with a spout serve hot brewed drinks at canteens and village halls

explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed drinks on tap' points to a pub's beer; the brew is the hot drink poured from a spigot.
explanation.definitionFit: Large metal containers with a tap that hold hot water or a brewed beverage for many cups.

explanation.surface: An invitation to an evening of dancing followed by a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively Scottish folk dance has this name, and when your head swims it spins or whirls.

parts.note: read as 'with this, a person is able to do things': the quality of being capable

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase sounds like 'one could make do with it', but it means that with this quality one can do things.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacity or skill is what lets a person accomplish a task.

parts.note: 'get it going' sounds like starting something up, but means receiving something as you leave

explanation.walkthrough: 'get it going' looks like starting an engine; here 'going' means leaving, and the present is handed over as a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A present given to someone departing a job or place, received at their leaving.

parts.note: the saying 'as poor as a' rodent living in a place of worship, where there is no food to steal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' reads as pity, but it means penniless: the proverbial creature with nothing to eat in a place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'poor as a ...' names this small rodent as the emblem of having nothing.

explanation.surface: Instructions to sprint without veering off course.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sprint is a run, and the punctuation mark is a short horizontal stroke.

indicators.note: taking action on the letters of the previous word sets them moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A recommendation of hasty measures for someone who never stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' signals rearranging PRECIPITATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling from place to place, as a wandering teacher or salesman does, is being itinerant.

explanation.surface: A cook told to shift the pot and give the sauce a few turns of the spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge or bestir oneself is to move, and turning a spoon round in a pot mixes its contents.

parts.note: 'habits' read as clothing, as a monk's habit: outfits worn for a formal meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' reads as routines, but a habit is also a garment, so these are clothes for dining.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal evening wear for men, a black tie outfit, is worn to a smart meal.

parts.note: 'late' means dead: the entrance to heaven, where Saint Peter waits

explanation.walkthrough: 'late entrants' suggests latecomers, but the late are the dead, entering heaven through its gateway.
explanation.definitionFit: In tradition the entrance to heaven is a gateway of pearl through which the dead pass.

clue.text: I'd learn about part of the British Isles

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the preceding letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A student promising to study one region of the islands off north-west Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells you to rearrange the letters of I'D LEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: The island west of Great Britain is geographically one of the British Isles.

clue.text: Boy of six embraced by his father

indicators.note: being embraced by someone means being held inside their arms, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A young lad being hugged by his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A common boy's name, borne by the biblical king.

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a steadfast barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow of blood or water is to dam it, and a firm, faithful supporter is loyal.

clue.text: Like a judge with robes in disarray

indicators.note: something in disarray is jumbled up, so the letters of the word before are mixed

explanation.surface: A judge whose official gown has come awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' signals rearranging ROBES. The saying 'as sober as a judge' gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'as sober as a judge' makes clear-headed and serious the quality of a judge.

clue.text: A green and mountainous part of France

explanation.surface: A traveller praising a lush, alpine French region.
explanation.definitionFit: A crinkly winter cabbage is a green vegetable of this name, and the Alpine region near Geneva is a mountainous French area.

clue.text: He ruled in one Roman era

indicators.note: in tells you the letters lie inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A remark on an emperor who held power for a single period of Roman history.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'oNE ROman era'. He was the emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman emperor of the first century was a ruler.

clue.text: Iago upset by cost of changing money

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the name are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's villain annoyed by the fee for a currency exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' signals rearranging IAGO, the schemer in Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: The premium charged when exchanging one currency for another, a banker's term.

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters gathered here are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone saying they were sent along to lend a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ME with AID (help).
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed or steered towards a target, as a weapon is aimed.

parts.note: the hard-working creatures are insects famed for diligence, and the heap is their nest of earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'industrious workers' suggests builders; the workers are insects whose nest is a mound of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of earth raised over a colony of small social insects, the workers of the nest.

clue.text: Very keen supporter voted out on two points

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: E is east, a compass point, taken twice

explanation.surface: An ardent fan dismissed from office on a pair of minor issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges VOTED to DEVOT; 'on' adds the two compass points E and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An enthusiast or ardent follower of a cause or person is a keen supporter.

clue.text: He's right to take Monday off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of the day are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man who is entitled to skip the start of the working week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the whole definition, a man's name; 'off' is the anagram signal, and 'take' just joins right to the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so the pronoun stands for him.

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps dusting and buffing a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Snubs or rejections are rebuffs, and read as 're-buffs' it means shines a second time.

explanation.surface: Something standing upright like a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The upas is a Javanese tree with a poisonous sap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Javanese tree with a poisonous milky sap, used for arrow poison.

indicators.note: here 'way out' means the way word is on the outside, so it wraps the other piece

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A business that has found an exit route along with a levy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'way out' as the way piece standing on the outside. The tax sense survives in 'scot-free', meaning without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a levy or payment, preserved in the phrase 'scot-free'.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Advice to watch when you raise your eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PEEK backwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a rule or custom is to observe it.

parts.note: the phrase means a respite, but read literally it is the organ in the chest where air is held

explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing space' usually means a pause; read literally it is an organ filled with air.
explanation.definitionFit: The spongy organ in the chest holding the air we inhale is a space for respiration.

clue.text: Coshed quite badly in the dance hall

indicators.note: badly means messily or wrongly, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A victim beaten up with a cosh at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges COSHED QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub for dancing to recorded music is a modern dance venue.

explanation.surface: Rules laid down for knockout football games.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonds or constraints are restrictions, and knockout games in a football cup competition are called by this name.

parts.note: the line is a washing line, and these clippers grip the laundry rather than cut anything

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clippers' suggests cutters, but these clip clothes to a washing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Little wooden or plastic clips fasten wet laundry to a washing line.
